# Unity Evidence and Safety

Detect Unity roots from Assets/Packages/ProjectSettings. Inspect the pinned Editor version, package manifests/locks, assemblies, scenes/prefabs, serialized configuration, startup/lifecycle, persistence, backend/native SDKs, platform settings, builds and tests when relevant. Exclude Library/Temp/Obj/Logs/Builds/UserSettings and dependency caches from documentation evidence.

Preserve serialized assets, GUIDs, package pins and unrelated work. Prefer Unity tooling for scene/asset changes. Never build generated solutions or run dotnet build without explicit authorization. Static inspection never establishes compilation, Play Mode, UI, player or device behavior.

Read the exact validation profile and repository authorization before Editor launch/tests. Approved Editor lifecycle includes only the stated checkout and selected task. A profile can cover graphical or headless/batchmode Editor import, compilation and named tests without implying a player build. Verify save/service isolation before gameplay or resets. Use one owned Editor/controller, record PID plus process start time and a hard deadline for every executed external operation, reserve cleanup time, preserve unrelated Editors from the current preflight and clean up only owned resources. Only the current preflight PID snapshot governs process ownership; other PID records supply evidence only. Inspect minimum process metadata; never retain full credential-bearing arguments, access tokens or secrets. Collect fresh assertions/logs/screenshots as required. Classify executed controls, prerequisite waits, transport uncertainties and host-policy rejections before updating counters. Record active controller time, tool wall time and prerequisite waiting separately. Do not create a cumulative root time pool. An optional total budget applies only to the selected task when concrete cost or irreversible risk justifies the limit; the task contract states charged time and stop behavior. Continue automatically with materially distinct evidence-backed controls inside standing scope. Stop the selected task after two consecutive executed controls produce the same unresolved failure without new evidence. No player build, device, package upgrade, external service or scheduling permission is implied.
